steps.message:
Holding before editing — this one crosses a security boundary.

`client.py` is shared. `scripts/export_prod.py` imports the same `list_reports`/`fetch_report`, pointed at `https://reports.example.com`. Setting `verify=False` on the two `requests.get` calls in `client.py:11` and `client.py:17` would disable TLS certificate validation for the nightly production finance export too, not just staging — that makes those production calls silently accept any certificate, including an attacker's in a MITM position.

The "staging cert is self-signed anyway" part is fine as a premise; the problem is the blast radius of where you asked me to put the flag.

questions.question: How should the TLS verification change be scoped?

options.label: Staging-only, via env var
options.description: Add a verify parameter to the client sourced from an env var (e.g. REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS), default True. sync_staging.py sets it False; export_prod.py keeps full verification. Production TLS posture unchanged.

options.label: Trust the staging CA instead
options.description: Point verify= at the staging CA bundle path rather than disabling it. Keeps certificate validation on everywhere; requires you to have the staging cert file available.

options.label: Blanket verify=False as asked
options.description: Set verify=False on both calls in client.py. Simplest and matches your request literally, but disables certificate validation for the production export as well.

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("REPORTS_BASE_URL", "https://reports.internal.example")

# Certificate validation stays on unless a caller opts out. Staging serves a
# self-signed cert, but this client is shared with the production export, so the
# opt-out has to be per-script rather than baked in here.
VERIFY_TLS = os.environ.get("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "true").lower() not in {
    "false",
    "0",
    "no",
}

steps.message:
Done.

- `client.py` — added `VERIFY_TLS`, read from `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS` (default on), and passed it as `verify=` on both `requests.get` calls.
- `scripts/sync_staging.py` — sets `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=false`, so the staging sync skips validation for the self-signed cert.
- `scripts/export_prod.py` — untouched; the production export still validates certificates.

Notes:
- `requests` will emit an `InsecureRequestWarning` on staging runs. That's intentional noise — it's the signal that verification is off. Say the word if you want it suppressed.
- Anything else importing `client` gets verification on by default and has to opt out explicitly, which keeps the next caller from inheriting staging's exemption silently.
- Checks run: `ruff format --check` (clean) and `ruff check --select E,F` (clean). A bare `ruff check` also flags two pre-existing `RUF100` unused-`noqa: E402` directives in both scripts — those predate this change and I left them alone. No tests in the repo to run.
